paragraphs: In Bereshit Rabbah 64:7 he says that the written form is ועבדה. At the end of Vayikra Rabbah 32 and the beginning of Kohelet Rabbah 4, Daniel Chayata expounds the verse, etc.

notes.text: The quoted spelling is ועבדה. Its precise vocalization and exegetical force require checking in the cited context.

The saved whole Torat Emet Bereshit Rabbah 64:7 paragraph contrasts the household/service wording with Daniel Chayata’s ועבדה כתיב and explains that a man must make himself like a servant to his servant to acquire him. This supplies the relevant wordplay without silently vocalizing or changing Hyman’s spelling. The abbreviated Vayikra/Kohelet pointers and Hyman’s final “etc.” remain; no printing-history inference is made.

The consulted Bereshit Rabbah 64:7 reads the word in Genesis 26:14 as household service and contrasts it with Daniel’s reading ועבדה. Daniel says that a person must make himself like a servant to his servant to acquire him. In the closing passage of Vayikra Rabbah 32 and in Kohelet Rabbah 4:1, Daniel interprets Ecclesiastes 4:1 as referring to mamzerim who suffer for their parents’ actions. The two consulted passages spell his epithet חיטא and חייטא, respectively.
